note: Adapted from Krishna & Adams (1982); only the soldier is described in the original (workers appear only in collection records), and the measurements are taken from the key (Table 4); plate descriptions and localities are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is distinctly larger than in L. buttel-reepeni and L. emersoni; the mandibles are longer, thinner and more strongly curved (especially the right mandible); the labrum is distinctly broader. Compared with buttel-reepeni, the sides of the head are more rounded (nearly parallel in that species); compared with emersoni, the mandibles are longer and the base of the labrum is broader.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head light brown, the anterior margin brown around the mandibles; postclypeus yellowish brown; antennae light brown; mandibles bright brown, fading basally to yellowish brown; labrum yellowish brown with the median lobe white and transparent. Sides of the head smooth and rounded. The basal half of the inner margin of the left mandible bears several successively smaller teeth, followed by fine serrations as far as the apex; the right mandible is strongly curved from base to apex, its inner margin nearly straight in dorsal view, with a narrow groove from the base to near the apex, extremely fine serrations along the lower edge of the groove, and a notch at the base above which lies a very small spine-like point. Antennae 12-segmented, segments 2, 3 and 4 subequal in length, the remaining segments longer. The anterior part of the postmentum is broadly oval, narrowing posteriorly to a minimum width and then widening again; constriction index 0.45–0.54. Pronotum about half as wide as the head, the anterior lobe slightly concave in the middle. Measurements: head length 1.15–1.28, maximum width 0.70–0.82, maximum height 0.65–0.70; right mandible 0.60–0.65, left mandible 0.64–0.72; postmentum length 0.78–0.87, maximum width 0.25–0.28, minimum width 0.12–0.15; pronotum maximum length 0.19–0.22, maximum width 0.35–0.40; hind tibia 0.55–0.63.
